+function Test-AzureFSRestoreToSecondaryRegion

+	$targetFileShareName = "afscrrtargetfs"
+
+	$vault = Get-AzRecoveryServicesVault -ResourceGroupName $resourceGroupName -Name $vaultName
+	Assert-NotNull $vault
+
+	$item = Get-AzRecoveryServicesBackupItem `
+		-VaultId $vault.ID `
+		-BackupManagementType AzureStorage `
+		-WorkloadType AzureFiles `
+		-FriendlyName $fileShareFriendlyName `
+		-UseSecondaryRegion
+	Assert-NotNull $item
+
+	# Anchor the query window on the item's LastBackupTime (a value that comes from the recorded item
+	# response). This keeps the request URL deterministic for playback, yet on a live re-record it tracks
+	# the current data automatically, so the window always brackets the available secondary recovery points.

+	$startDate = $anchor.AddDays(-30)
+	$endDate = $anchor.AddDays(1)

+		-VaultId $vault.ID `
+		-Item $item `
+		-StartDate $startDate -EndDate $endDate `
+		-UseSecondaryRegion
+	Assert-NotNull $rp
+	Assert-True { @($rp).Count -gt 0 }
+
+	# VARIATION-1: CRR requires ALR — omitting the target storage account must throw
+	Assert-ThrowsContains `
+		{ Restore-AzRecoveryServicesBackupItem `
+			-VaultId $vault.ID -VaultLocation $vault.Location `
+			-RecoveryPoint $rp[0] -ResolveConflict Overwrite -RestoreToSecondaryRegion -ErrorAction Stop } `
+		"Alternate Location Restore"
+
+	# VARIATION-2: CRR does not support item-level restore — passing -SourceFilePath must throw
+	Assert-ThrowsContains `

+			-RecoveryPoint $rp[0] `
+			-TargetStorageAccountName $targetStorageAccountName `
+			-TargetFileShareName $targetFileShareName `
+			-SourceFilePath "somefile.txt" -SourceFileType File `
+			-ResolveConflict Overwrite -RestoreToSecondaryRegion -ErrorAction Stop } `
+		"Item-level restore is not supported"
+
+	# VARIATION-3: full CRR restore to secondary region completes.
+	$crrJob = Restore-AzRecoveryServicesBackupItem `
+		-VaultId $vault.ID -VaultLocation $vault.Location `

+		-TargetStorageAccountName $targetStorageAccountName `
+		-TargetFileShareName $targetFileShareName `

+		-RestoreToSecondaryRegion

discussion_comments.comment_body:
This is another change introduced in AutoRest v4, where IdentityType has been updated.
Previously, there were two properties: IdentityType and IdentityUserAssignedIdentity. The IdentityType property indicated whether SystemAssigned and/or UserAssigned identities were used.

In v4, this has been changed. We now use EnableSystemAssignedIdentity to indicate SystemAssigned identity. If it is enabled, SystemAssigned identity is used.
Additionally, UserAssignedIdentity is now a string array. If it contains values, it means UserAssigned identities are being used.

For more information, please see: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2340249

-        [System.String]

+        [System.Management.Automation.SwitchParameter]
+        ${EnableSystemAssignedIdentity},
discussion_comments.comment_body:
In v4 of the AutoRest generator, IdentityType is modeled as a nullable enum behind the new SwitchParameter.

Previously in v3 we explicitly passed "None" as a string value. In v4, the equivalent behavior is achieved by not passing the switch parameter at all, which results in no identity being configured (effectively the same as None).

So there isn’t a regression in functionality — the representation just changed from a string value ("None") to the absence of the switch.

Regarding userAssignedIdentityId:

In AutoRest v4 the generated type has changed from Hashtable to System.String[]. This is a generator-side breaking change compared to v3.

AutoRest will not automatically convert a Hashtable into String[] during serialization. The generated client now expects an array of resource IDs, so the service contract needs to align with this updated shape. This requires an update on the service side.

This change is part of the AutoRest v4 identity modeling updates. For additional details, please refer to the official guidance:
https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2340249
